cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(lgl-system-loadout VERSION 2.1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
# C++17 is used rather than C++20 (the preferred standard) because compiling
# Qt6 headers in C++20 mode activates C++20-specific Qt code paths that
# reference symbols only present in Qt 6.10+, breaking compatibility with
# the Qt6 version shipped on Fedora 43+ target systems.
set(CMAKE_AUTOMOC ON)
set(CMAKE_AUTORCC ON)

# Treat warnings as errors on GCC and Clang (dev standard requirement).
if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
    add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Werror)
endif()

# Enable AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer for Debug builds.
# ThreadSanitizer is mutually exclusive with ASan — use -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=TSan.
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
        add_compile_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
        add_link_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined)
    endif()
elseif(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "TSan")
    if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
        add_compile_options(-g -O1 -fsanitize=thread -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
        add_link_options(-fsanitize=thread)
    endif()
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GUI application — Qt Widgets, runs as the normal user (never root).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Core Widgets Concurrent)

qt_add_executable(lgl-system-loadout
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/main.cpp
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pagehelpers.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/mainwizard.cpp            ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/mainwizard.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/installworker.cpp         ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/installworker.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/updatepage.cpp      ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/updatepage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/welcomepage.cpp     ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/welcomepage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/repospage.cpp       ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/repospage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/systemtoolspage.cpp ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/systemtoolspage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/pythonpage.cpp      ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/pythonpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/multimediapage.cpp  ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/multimediapage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/contentpage.cpp     ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/contentpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/gpupage.cpp         ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/gpupage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/gamingpage.cpp      ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/gamingpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/virtpage.cpp        ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/virtpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/browserspage.cpp    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/browserspage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/commspage.cpp       ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/commspage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/cachyospage.cpp     ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/cachyospage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/lgltoolkitpage.cpp  ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/lgltoolkitpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/reviewpage.cpp      ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/reviewpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/installpage.cpp  ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/installpage.h
    ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/donepage.cpp        ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pages/donepage.h
)

target_link_libraries(lgl-system-loadout PRIVATE Qt6::Core Qt6::Widgets Qt6::Concurrent Qt6::Network)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Privileged helper — Qt Core only, no Widgets dependency.
# Installed to /usr/libexec/lgl-system-loadout/ (FHS location for helpers).
# Launched exclusively via pkexec — never run directly by the user.

)

62	// detectSystem() runs synchronously in the constructor, before the window is shown.
63	// This is an accepted startup probe: it invokes only fast local binaries (rpm, logname)
64	// with strict timeouts (≤3 s). It must never make network calls or invoke dnf.
65	// If either binary hangs beyond its timeout it is killed and a safe default is used.
66	void MainWizard::detectSystem()
67	{
68	    {
69	        QProcess p;
70	        p.start("rpm", {"-E", "%fedora"});
71	        if (!p.waitForFinished(3000)) p.kill();
72	        m_fedoraVersion = QString::fromUtf8(p.readAllStandardOutput()).trimmed();
73	        if (m_fedoraVersion.isEmpty() || m_fedoraVersion.startsWith('%'))
74	            m_fedoraVersion = "44";
75	    }
76	    {
77	        // targetUser is passed as an argument to usermod and as context for
78	        // user-scoped tools. Validate immediately — only lowercase POSIX usernames
79	        // accepted. Anything else results in a "root" fallback with a warning.
80	        static const QRegularExpression kSafeUsername(
81	            QStringLiteral("^[a-z_][a-z0-9_\\-]{0,31}$"));
82	
83	        auto isSafeUsername = [&](const QString &name) -> bool {
84	            return !name.isEmpty()
85	                && name != QStringLiteral("root")
86	                && kSafeUsername.match(name).hasMatch();
87	        };
88	
89	        m_targetUser = qEnvironmentVariable("SUDO_USER");
90	        if (!isSafeUsername(m_targetUser)) {
91	            QProcess p;
92	            p.start("logname", {});
93	            if (!p.waitForFinished(2000)) p.kill();
94	            m_targetUser = QString::fromUtf8(p.readAllStandardOutput()).trimmed();
95	        }
96	        if (!isSafeUsername(m_targetUser)) {
97	            qWarning() << "detectSystem: could not determine a safe non-root target user "
98	                          "(SUDO_USER unset or invalid, logname returned nothing useful). "
99	                          "Falling back to 'root'. User-scoped tools (pipx, kpackagetool6) "
100	                          "will run as root.";
101	            m_targetUser = "root";
102	        }
103	    }
104	}

109	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
110	// Launch the privileged helper
111	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
112	QString MainWizard::launchHelper()
113	{
114	    // Guard: only launch once per session.
115	    if (m_helperProcess && m_helperProcess->state() == QProcess::Running)
116	        return m_opts.value("install/socketPath").toString();
117	
118	    // Attempt to launch the helper, retrying once after a short delay.
119	    // On first launch from Discover post-install, the D-Bus session may not
120	    // be ready to handle pkexec authentication. A single silent retry after
121	    // 1.5 s covers this without the user ever seeing an error.
122	    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 2; ++attempt) {
123	        if (attempt > 0) {
124	            // Wait 1.5 s before retrying without blocking the UI thread.
125	            QEventLoop loop;
126	            QTimer::singleShot(1500, &loop, &QEventLoop::quit);
127	            loop.exec();
128	        }
129	
130	        delete m_helperProcess;
131	        m_helperProcess = new QProcess(this);
132	        m_helperProcess->setProcessChannelMode(QProcess::SeparateChannels);
133	        m_helperProcess->start("pkexec",
134	            {"/usr/libexec/lgl-system-loadout/lgl-system-loadout-helper"});
135	
136	        if (!m_helperProcess->waitForStarted(10000)) {
137	            delete m_helperProcess;
138	            m_helperProcess = nullptr;
139	            continue;
140	        }
141	
142	        QString socketPath;
143	        if (m_helperProcess->waitForReadyRead(60000))
144	            socketPath = QString::fromLocal8Bit(m_helperProcess->readLine()).trimmed();
145	
146	        if (!socketPath.isEmpty() && socketPath.startsWith("/run/lgl-")) {
147	            m_opts["install/socketPath"] = socketPath;
148	            return socketPath;
149	        }
150	
151	        qWarning() << "lgl-helper launch attempt" << (attempt + 1) << "failed."
152	                   << "pkexec stderr:" << m_helperProcess->readAllStandardError()
153	                   << "exit code:" << m_helperProcess->exitCode();
154	        m_helperProcess->kill();
155	        delete m_helperProcess;
156	        m_helperProcess = nullptr;
157	    }
158	
159	    return {};
160	}
161

535	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
536	// Run a single command via the helper, streaming output to a callback.
537	// Launches the helper if not already running.
538	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
539	int MainWizard::runHelperCommand(const QStringList &command,
540	                                 std::function<void(const QString &)> outputLine)
541	{
542	    // Helper must already be launched via launchHelper() on the main thread
543	    // before calling this function. launchHelper() must never be called from
544	    // a worker thread as it creates a QProcess parented to MainWizard.
545	    const QString socketPath = m_opts.value("install/socketPath").toString();
546	    if (socketPath.isEmpty()) {
547	        outputLine("ERROR: helper not launched — call launchHelper() first");
548	        return -1;
549	    }
550	
551	    QLocalSocket sock;
552	    sock.connectToServer(socketPath);
553	    if (!sock.waitForConnected(5000)) {
554	        outputLine(QString("ERROR: could not connect to helper: %1")
555	                   .arg(sock.errorString()));
556	        return -1;
557	    }
558	
559	    static int s_counter = 0;
560	    const QString requestId = QString("main-%1").arg(++s_counter);
561	
562	    QJsonObject msg;
563	    msg["type"]      = "execute";
564	    msg["requestId"] = requestId;
565	    msg["program"]   = command.first();
566	    QJsonArray args;
567	    for (int i = 1; i < command.size(); ++i) args.append(command[i]);
568	    msg["args"] = args;
569	
570	    QByteArray data = QJsonDocument(msg).toJson(QJsonDocument::Compact);
571	    data.append('\n');
572	    sock.write(data);
573	    sock.flush();
574	
575	    QByteArray readBuf;
576	    int result = -1;
577	
578	    while (true) {
579	        if (!sock.waitForReadyRead(500)) {
580	            if (sock.state() != QLocalSocket::ConnectedState) {
581	                outputLine("ERROR: helper disconnected unexpectedly");
582	                break;
583	            }
584	            continue;
585	        }
586	
587	        readBuf.append(sock.readAll());
588	
589	        int newline;
590	        while ((newline = readBuf.indexOf('\n')) != -1) {
591	            const QByteArray raw = readBuf.left(newline).trimmed();
592	            readBuf.remove(0, newline + 1);
593	            if (raw.isEmpty()) continue;
594	
595	            QJsonParseError parseErr;
596	            const QJsonDocument doc = QJsonDocument::fromJson(raw, &parseErr);
597	            if (parseErr.error != QJsonParseError::NoError || !doc.isObject()) continue;
598	
599	            const QJsonObject resp = doc.object();
600	            const QString     type = resp["type"].toString();
601	
602	            if (type == "output") {
603	                outputLine(resp["line"].toString());
604	            } else if (type == "finished") {
605	                result = resp["exitCode"].toInt(-1);
606	                goto done; // NOLINT
607	            } else if (type == "rejected") {
608	                outputLine(QString("ERROR: helper rejected: %1").arg(resp["error"].toString()));
609	                goto done; // NOLINT
610	            } else if (type == "error") {
611	                outputLine(QString("ERROR: %1").arg(resp["error"].toString()));
612	                goto done; // NOLINT
613	            }
614	        }
615	    }
616	
617	done:
618	    sock.disconnectFromServer();
619	    return result;
620	}

724	int MainWizard::availableDiskMB()
725	{
726	    QProcess p;
727	    p.start("df", {"--output=avail", "-m", "/"});
728	    if (!p.waitForFinished(3000)) { p.kill(); return -1; }
729	    const QStringList lines = QString::fromUtf8(p.readAllStandardOutput())
730	                                .trimmed().split('\n');
731	    if (lines.size() >= 2) {
732	        bool ok;
733	        int avail = lines.last().trimmed().toInt(&ok);
734	        if (ok) return avail;
735	    }
736	    return -1;
737	}

21	// Copies text to the clipboard, setting both Clipboard and Selection modes
22	// for reliable behaviour across Wayland and X11.
23	inline void copyToClipboard(const QString &text)
24	{
25	    auto *md = new QMimeData;
26	    md->setText(text);
27	    QApplication::clipboard()->setMimeData(md, QClipboard::Clipboard);
28	    if (QApplication::clipboard()->supportsSelection()) {
29	        auto *mdSel = new QMimeData;
30	        mdSel->setText(text);
31	        QApplication::clipboard()->setMimeData(mdSel, QClipboard::Selection);
32	    }
33	}

35	// ---- Smooth scrolling QScrollArea ----
36	// Fixes mouse wheel scroll being intercepted by the wizard navigation.
37	// Installs an event filter on every descendant so wheel events are always
38	// caught regardless of which child widget the cursor is over.
39	class SmoothScrollArea : public QScrollArea
40	{
41	public:
42	    explicit SmoothScrollArea(QWidget *parent = nullptr) : QScrollArea(parent)
43	    {
44	        setFocusPolicy(Qt::WheelFocus);
45	        setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(Qt::ScrollBarAlwaysOff);
46	        setVerticalScrollBarPolicy(Qt::ScrollBarAsNeeded);
47	        setWidgetResizable(true);
48	    }
49	
50	    void setWidget(QWidget *w)
51	    {
52	        QScrollArea::setWidget(w);
53	        if (w) installOnAll(w);
54	    }
55	
56	private:
57	    void installOnAll(QObject *obj)
58	    {
59	        obj->installEventFilter(this);
60	        for (QObject *child : obj->children())
61	            installOnAll(child);
62	    }
63	
64	    void doScroll(QWheelEvent *we)
65	    {
66	        QScrollBar *vbar = verticalScrollBar();
67	        int px = we->pixelDelta().y();
68	        if (px != 0) {
69	            vbar->setValue(vbar->value() - px);
70	        } else {
71	            int delta = we->angleDelta().y();
72	            // angleDelta is in units of 1/8 degree; one notch = 120 units (15 degrees).
73	            // Use rounding division to avoid silent truncation on odd delta values.
74	            vbar->setValue(vbar->value() - (delta * 60 + (delta >= 0 ? 60 : -60)) / 120);
75	        }
76	    }
77	
78	protected:
79	    void wheelEvent(QWheelEvent *e) override
80	    {
81	        doScroll(e);
82	        e->accept();
83	    }
84	
85	    bool eventFilter(QObject *obj, QEvent *e) override
86	    {
87	        if (e->type() == QEvent::Wheel) {
88	            doScroll(static_cast<QWheelEvent*>(e));
89	            e->accept();
90	            return true;
91	        }
92	        // When new child widgets are added after setWidget(), catch them too
93	        if (e->type() == QEvent::ChildAdded) {
94	            QChildEvent *ce = static_cast<QChildEvent*>(e);
95	            if (ce->child()) installOnAll(ce->child());
96	        }
97	        return QScrollArea::eventFilter(obj, e);
98	    }
99	};

103	// Uses dnf list --installed for reliable detection even when rpm -q is ambiguous
104	inline bool isDnfInstalled(const QString &pkg)
105	{
106	    QProcess p;
107	    p.setProgram("/usr/bin/rpm");
108	    p.setArguments({"-q", "--quiet", pkg});
109	    p.start();
110	    p.waitForFinished(-1);  // no timeout — rpm is always fast, never hangs
111	    return p.exitCode() == 0;

192	// ---- Async badge checker ----
193	// Runs a list of check functions concurrently in a thread pool,
194	// then calls `onDone(results)` on the main thread when all are complete.
195	// This eliminates the per-page lag caused by sequential rpm -q calls.
196	//
197	// Usage:
198	//   runChecksAsync(this, {
199	//       {"steam",  []{ return isDnfInstalled("steam"); }},
200	//       {"heroic", []{ return isFlatpakInstalled("com.heroicgameslauncher.hgl"); }},
201	//   }, [this](QMap<QString,bool> r) {
202	//       // called on main thread - populate badges here
203	//       m_boxes["steam"]->setProperty("installed", r["steam"]);
204	//   });
205	#include <QPointer>
206	
207	inline void runChecksAsync(
208	    QObject *context,
209	    QList<QPair<QString, std::function<bool()>>> checks,
210	    std::function<void(QMap<QString,bool>)> onDone)
211	{
212	    auto *watcher = new QFutureWatcher<QMap<QString,bool>>();
213	    // Guard against context being destroyed before the finished signal fires.
214	    // If the context QObject is deleted (e.g. page navigation), the callback is
215	    // a no-op rather than a use-after-free.
216	    QPointer<QObject> guard(context);
217	    QObject::connect(watcher, &QFutureWatcher<QMap<QString,bool>>::finished,
218	        context, [watcher, onDone, guard]() {
219	            if (guard) onDone(watcher->result());
220	            watcher->deleteLater();
221	        });
222	    auto future = QtConcurrent::run([checks]() -> QMap<QString,bool> {
223	        // Run checks sequentially — concurrent rpm processes can interfere
224	        // with each other causing silent failures on some systems.
225	        QMap<QString,bool> results;
226	        for (const auto &item : checks)
227	            results[item.first] = item.second();
228	        return results;
229	    });
230	    watcher->setFuture(future);
231	}
232	inline QCheckBox* makeItemRow(QWidget *parent, QLayout *layout,
233	                              const QString &label,
234	                              bool installed,
235	                              bool showBadge = true)
236	{
237	    auto *row    = new QWidget(parent);
238	    auto *rowLay = new QHBoxLayout(row);
239	    rowLay->setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0);
240	    rowLay->setSpacing(8);
241	
242	    auto *cb = new QCheckBox(label, row);
243	    rowLay->addWidget(cb, 1);
244	
245	    if (showBadge) {
246	        auto *badge = new QLabel(installed ? "[Installed]" : "[Not Installed]", row);
247	        badge->setObjectName("badge");
248	        badge->setMinimumWidth(110);
249	        badge->setAlignment(Qt::AlignRight | Qt::AlignVCenter);
250	        badge->setStyleSheet(installed
251	            ? "color: #3db03d; font-weight: bold; font-size: 8pt;"
252	            : "color: #cc7700; font-weight: bold; font-size: 8pt;");
253	        rowLay->addWidget(badge);
254	    }
255	
256	    layout->addWidget(row);
257	    return cb;
258	}
259	
260	// Toolbar button helper - consistent sizing that adapts to theme font
261	inline QPushButton* makeToolbarBtn(const QString &text, QWidget *parent = nullptr)
262	{
263	    auto *btn = new QPushButton(text, parent);
264	    btn->setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy::Minimum, QSizePolicy::Fixed);
265	    btn->setMinimumWidth(btn->fontMetrics().horizontalAdvance(text) + 24);
266	    return btn;
267	}
268	
269	// Description label that reads well on both light and dark themes
270	inline QLabel* makeDescLabel(QWidget *parent, const QString &desc)
271	{
272	    auto *dl = new QLabel("    " + desc, parent);
273	    dl->setWordWrap(true);
274	    auto pal = dl->palette();
275	    auto c = pal.color(QPalette::WindowText);
276	    c.setAlphaF(0.55f);
277	    pal.setColor(QPalette::WindowText, c);
278	    dl->setPalette(pal);
279	    return dl;
280	}

3	# The LGL System Loadout
4	
5	**Get a fresh Fedora install ready for gaming, content creation, and development — without the terminal.**
6	
7	[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
8	[![Fedora](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fedora-43%20%7C%2044-blue?logo=fedora&logoColor=white)](https://fedoraproject.org)
9	[![Qt](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qt-6-green?logo=qt&logoColor=white)](https://www.qt.io)
10	<p align="center">
11	  <a href="https://ko-fi.com/G2G3V70LW">
12	    <img src="https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/kofi6.png?v=6" height="36" alt="Buy Me a Coffee at ko-fi.com" />
13	  </a>
14	</p>
15	</div>
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Overview
20	
21	LGL System Loadout is a graphical setup wizard for Fedora. Pick exactly what you want from a curated list of software across gaming, multimedia, content creation, development, browsers, communication, GPU drivers, virtualisation, and the CachyOS kernel. One password prompt covers the entire installation.
22	
23	- Nothing is selected by default — every choice is yours
24	- Every item shows its current installed state before you commit
25	- Installs only — nothing is removed without your knowledge
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Install
30	
31	### Recommended — COPR
32	
33	```bash
34	sudo dnf copr enable linuxgamerlife/lgl-system-loadout
35	sudo dnf install lgl-system-loadout
36	```
37	
38	Launch **LGL System Loadout** from your application menu.
39	
40	### No Terminal — RPM from Releases
41	
42	Download the `.rpm` for your Fedora version from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/linuxgamerlife/lgl-system-loadout/releases) and double-click to install via Discover.
43	
44	- `lgl-system-loadout-2.1.0-1.fc43.x86_64.rpm` — Fedora 43
45	- `lgl-system-loadout-2.1.0-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm` — Fedora 44
46	
47	> After installing from Discover, close it and launch the app from your application menu rather than from the Discover install screen.
48	
49	### Polkit
50	If you are using this in KDE, Workstation or another spin, then authentication will be baked in. If you are building out your Fedora install without a Desktop Environment to start and using Noctalia as your shell, you will need a polkit service. I would recommend the Noctalia built in one which is in in Noctalia  `Settings > Security > Polkit`
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Build from Source
55	
56	```bash
57	# Install build dependencies
58	sudo dnf install cmake gcc-c++ qt6-qtbase-devel
59	
60	# Clone and build
61	git clone https://github.com/linuxgamerlife/lgl-system-loadout.git
62	cd lgl-system-loadout
63	mkdir build && cd build
64	cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
65	make -j$(nproc)
66	```
67	
68	> Always build on the same machine you intend to run on. If you see `version 'Qt_6.x' not found`, run `sudo dnf upgrade qt6-qtbase` first.
69

```
1	<img src="https://github.com/nwg-piotr/nwg-look/assets/20579136/c2a6244b-4eae-489e-b9bc-272347238be8" width="90" style="margin-right:10px" align=left alt="logo">
2	<H1>nwg-look</H1><br>
3	
4	This application is a part of the [nwg-shell](https://nwg-piotr.github.io/nwg-shell) project.
5	
6	Nwg-look is a GTK settings editor, designed to work properly in wlroots-based Wayland environment.
7	The look and feel is strongly influenced by [LXAppearance](https://wiki.lxde.org/en/LXAppearance),
8	but nwg-look is intended to free the user from a few inconveniences:
9	
10	- It works natively on Wayland. You no longer need Xwayland, nor strange env variables for it to run.
11	- It applies gsettings directly, with no need to use
12	[workarounds](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/wiki/GTK-3-settings-on-Wayland). You don't need to set
13	 gsettings in the sway config file. You don't need the `import-gsettings` script.
14	
15	![nwg-look](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwg-piotr/nwg-shell-resources/master/images/nwg-look/nwg-look-0.1.3.png)
16	
17	## Dependencies
18	
19	- go (build dependency)
20	- gtk3
21	- [xcur2png](https://github.com/eworm-de/xcur2png)
22	- gsettings
23	
24	Depending on your distro, you may also need to install
25	[gotk3 dependencies](https://github.com/gotk3/gotk3#installation).
26	
27	## Installation
28	
29	[![Packaging status](https://repology.org/badge/vertical-allrepos/nwg-look.svg)](https://repology.org/project/nwg-look/versions)
30	
31	If nwg-look has not yet been packaged for your Linux distribution:
32	
33	1. Clone the repository, cd into it.
34	2. `make build`
35	3. `sudo make install`
36	
37	## Usage
38	
39	```text
40	$ nwg-look -h
41	Usage of nwg-look:
42	  -a	Apply stored gsetting and quit
43	  -d	turn on Debug messages
44	  -r	Restore default values and quit
45	  -v	display Version information
46	  -x	eXport config files and quit
47	```
48	
49	The `-a` flag has been added just in case. When you press the "Apply" button, in addition to applying the changes, a backup file is also created. You may apply gsetting again w/o running the GUI, by just `nwg-look -a`. No idea if it's going to be useful in real life. ;)
50	
51	### Usage in sway
52	
53	The default way to apply GTK setting on [sway](https://github.com/swaywm/sway) Wayland compositor has been
54	described in the [GTK 3 settings on Wayland](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/wiki/GTK-3-settings-on-Wayland)
55	Wiki section. **You no longer need it**. Nwg-look loads and saves gsettings values directly, and does not
56	care about the `~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini` file. It only exports your settings to it, unless you use
57	the `-n` flag.
58	
59	Therefore, if your sway config file contains either
60	
61	```text
62	set $gnome-schema org.gnome.desktop.interface
63	
64	exec_always {
65	    gsettings set $gnome-schema gtk-theme 'Your theme'
66	    gsettings set $gnome-schema icon-theme 'Your icon theme'
67	    gsettings set $gnome-schema cursor-theme 'Your cursor Theme'
68	    gsettings set $gnome-schema font-name 'Your font name'
69	}
70	```
71	
72	or if you use the `import-gsettings` script:
73	
74	```text
75	exec_always import-gsettings
76	```
77	
78	to parse and apply the settings.ini file, **remove these lines**.
79	
80	## Backward compatibility
81	
82	Some gsetting keys have no direct counterparts in the Gtk.Settings type. While exporting
83	the settings.ini file, nwg-look uses the most similar values:
84	
85	| gsettings | Gtk.Settings |
86	| --------- | ------------ |
87	| `font-hinting` | `gtk-xft-hintstyle` |
88	| `font-antialiasing` | `gtk-xft-antialias` |
89	| `font-rgba-order` | `gtk-xft-rgba` |
90	
91	Some **Other** settings have been left just for LXAppearance compatibility, and possible
92	use of your settings.ini file elsewhere:
93	
94	- Toolbar style
95	- Toolbar icon size
96	
97	have been deprecated since GTK 3.10, and the values are ignored.
98	
99	- Show button images
100	- Show menu images
101	
102	have been deprecated since GTK 3.10, and have no corresponding gsettings values.
103	
104	- Enable event sounds
105	- Enable input feedback sounds
106	
107	don't seem to change anything in non-GNOME environment.
```

# For alternate install dir (e.g. "/usr/local")
# specify PREFIX in make command:
#   sudo make PREFIX=/usr/local install
# Defaults to "/usr" if not specified.
PREFIX ?= /usr

get:
	go get github.com/gotk3/gotk3
	go get github.com/gotk3/gotk3/gdk
	go get "github.com/sirupsen/logrus"

build:
	go build -v -o bin/nwg-look .

install:
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/nwg-look
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/nwg-look/langs
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/applications
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/pixmaps

	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/doc/nwg-look
	mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/licenses/nwg-look

	cp stuff/main.glade $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/nwg-look/
	cp langs/* $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/nwg-look/langs/
	cp stuff/nwg-look.desktop $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/applications/
	cp stuff/nwg-look.svg $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/pixmaps/
	cp bin/nwg-look $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin

	cp README.md $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/doc/nwg-look
	cp LICENSE $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/licenses/nwg-look

uninstall:
	rm -r $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/nwg-look
	rm $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/applications/nwg-look.desktop
	rm $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/pixmaps/nwg-look.svg
	rm $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin/nwg-look

run:
	go run .

495	func applyGsettingsFromFile() {
496		gsettingsFile := filepath.Join(dataHome(), "nwg-look/gsettings")
497		if pathExists(gsettingsFile) {
498			log.Infof("Loading gsettings from %s", gsettingsFile)
499			lines, err := loadTextFile(gsettingsFile)
500			if err != nil {
501				log.Fatalf("Failed loading file: %s", err)
502			}
503			var key, value string
504			for _, line := range lines {
505				if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
506					parts := strings.Split(line, "=")
507					if len(parts) == 2 {
508						key = parts[0]
509						value = parts[1]
510	
511						switch key {
512						case "gtk-theme":
513							gsettings.gtkTheme = value
514						case "icon-theme":
515							gsettings.iconTheme = value
516						case "font-name":
517							gsettings.fontName = value
518						case "cursor-theme":
519							gsettings.cursorTheme = value
520						case "cursor-size":
521							v, err := strconv.Atoi(value)
522							if err == nil {
523								gsettings.cursorSize = v
524							}
525						case "toolbar-style":
526							gsettings.toolbarStyle = value
527						case "toolbar-icons-size":
528							gsettings.toolbarIconsSize = value
529						case "font-hinting":
530							gsettings.fontHinting = value
531						case "font-antialiasing":
532							gsettings.fontAntialiasing = value
533						case "font-rgba-order":
534							gsettings.fontRgbaOrder = value
535						case "text-scaling-factor":
536							v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(value, 64)
537							if err == nil {
538								gsettings.textScalingFactor = v
539							}
540						case "event-sounds":
541							gsettings.eventSounds = value == "true"
542						case "input-feedback-sounds":
543							gsettings.inputFeedbackSounds = value == "true"
544						case "color-scheme":
545							gsettings.colorScheme = value
546						}
547					}
548				}
549			}
550			applyGsettings()
551		} else {
552			log.Warnf("Couldn't find file: %s", gsettingsFile)
553			os.Exit(1)
554		}
555	}

1	qt6ct - Qt6 Configuration Tool
2	
3	This program allows users to configure Qt6 settings (theme, font, icons, etc.)
4	under DE/WM without Qt integration.
5	
6	Official home page: https://github.com/trialuser02/qt6ct
7	
8	Requirements:
9	
10	- GNU Linux or FreeBSD
11	- qtbase >= 6.0.0
12	- qtsvg >= 6.0.0 (Runtime dependency for the SVG icon support)
13	- qttools >= 6.0.0 (For build only)
14	
15	
16	Installation:
17	
18	- Arch package
19	  https://archlinux.org/packages/?q=qt6ct
20	
21	- Source Code (qmake)
22	  qmake PREFIX=<your installation path>
23	  make
24	  sudo make install
25	
26	- Source Code (cmake)
27	  cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=<your installation path>
28	  make
29	  sudo make install
30	
31	Add line 'export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct' to ~/.profile and re-login.
32	Alternatively, create the file /etc/X11/Xsession.d/100-qt6ct with
33	the following line:
34	
35	export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct
36	
37	(or qt5ct for compatibility with Qt5 Configuration Tool)
38	
39	Now restart X11 server to take the changes effect.
40	
41	Extra build options (for advanced users only):
42	qmake DISABLE_WIDGETS=1 - compiles platform plugin without QtWidgets (useful for QML applications only)
43	qmake PLUGINDIR=<custom path> - changes the default installation path of the plugins (libqt6ct.so and libqt6ct-style.so)
44	
45	Wayland:
46	
47	If you are running Qt application under Wayland, you should export the following variables:
48	
49	export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland
50	export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct
51	
52	Debug Messages:
53	
54	By default, debug messages from platform plugin are disabled. To enable them, you should
55	export the following environment variable:
56	
57	export QT_LOGGING_RULES="qt6ct.debug=true"
58	
59	Another way is to change qtlogging.ini file. See Qt documentation for details:
60	https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qloggingcategory.html (paragraph "Configuring Categories")
61	
62	Files and Directories:
63	
64	qt6ct - Qt6 configuration tool
65	libqt6ct.so - qt6ct platform plugin
66	libqt6ct-style.so - qt6ct proxy style plugin
67	libqt6ct-common.so - qt6ct shared library
68	~/.config/qt6ct/qt6ct.conf - configuration file
69	~/.config/qt6ct/qss, ~/.local/share/qt6ct/qss, /usr/share/qt6ct/qss, /usr/local/share/qt6ct/qss - style sheets
70	~/.config/qt6ct/colors,~/.local/share/qt6ct/colors, /usr/share/qt6ct/colors,
71	/usr/local/share/qt6ct/colors - color schemes
72	/etc/xdg/qt6ct/qt6ct.conf - default configuration file

# KineticWE

> **This repository is a fork of [KWin](https://github.com/KDE/kwin) from the [KDE](https://kde.org) project.**
>
> KineticWE adds native tiling support while keeping the Destktop Enviroment Feel.**KineticWE** — a KWin Window Environment that pairs the [Noctalia](https://github.com/noctalia-dev/noctalia) shell with this compositor.


## ❤ Support the Project

If you want to support this project, you can donate here: [Ko-fi — theblackdon](https://ko-fi.com/theblackdon)

---

> ## ⚠ BETA Stage
>
> **KineticWE is currently in BETA.**
>
> Expect:
> - Bugs, crashes, and visual glitches.
> - Breaking changes between commits (config keys, scripts, CLI flags).
> - Features that work today may be removed or rewritten tomorrow.
>
> Please do **note** use KineticWE as your daily driver on a production system. Feedback and bug reports are welcome, but you are running pre-release software.

> # LLM-Generated Code Disclaimer
>
> Portions of this project — including (but not limited to) installer scripts, build glue, configuration files, documentation, and some C++/QML/JS source files — were **authored with the assistance of LLM tools** (large language models coding assistants).
>
> All LLM-generated content has been reviewed by the maintainers, but it has **not** been audited to the same standard as hand-written code. You may encounter:
> - Subtle bugs or edge cases that a human author would have caught.
> - Stylistic inconsistencies with the surrounding KWin codebase.
>
> **If you are not comfortable running code that was written (in whole or in part) by an LLM, do not use this project and keep it movin.** By using KineticWE you acknowledge and accept this.

---

## Installing KineticWE

### COPR (Fedora) — Recommended - Use Fedora Linux for the best and tested experience

The recommended way to install KineticWE on Fedora is via [COPR](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/).
COPR provides pre-built RPMs so you don't need to compile from source.

Enable the required COPR repositories, then install:

```bash
sudo dnf copr enable lionheartp/Hyprland
sudo dnf copr enable theblackdon/kineticwe
sudo dnf install kineticwe noctalia-git
```

After installation, select **KineticWE** from your display manager's session menu
or run `start-kineticwe` from a TTY.

The `kineticwe` package provides and obsoletes Fedora's stock `kwin`, `kwin-common`,
`kwin-libs`, `kglobalacceld`, and `kdecoration` packages — it replaces the stock
compositor rather than installing alongside it.

> **Note:** The first time you install, reboot before logging in to a KineticWE session. On subsequent logins Noctalia will load automatically.
>

    QPlatformTheme *create(const QString &key, const QStringList &params) override;
};

QPlatformTheme *Qt6CTPlatformThemePlugin::create(const QString &key, const QStringList &params)
{
    Q_UNUSED(params);
    QVersionNumber v = QLibraryInfo::version();
    if(v.majorVersion() != QT_VERSION_MAJOR || v.minorVersion() != QT_VERSION_MINOR)
    {
        qCCritical(lqt6ct) << "qt6ct is compiled against incompatible Qt version (" QT_VERSION_STR ").";
        return nullptr;
    }

    if(key.toLower() == QLatin1String("qt6ct") || key.toLower() == QLatin1String("qt5ct"))
        return new Qt6CTPlatformTheme();
    return nullptr;
}

QT_END_NAMESPACE

func getCursorThemes() (map[string]string, map[string]string) {
	var dirs []string
	name2path := make(map[string]string)
	name2FolderName := make(map[string]string)

	// get icon theme dirs
	for _, dir := range dataDirs {
		if pathExists(filepath.Join(dir, "icons")) {
			dirs = append(dirs, filepath.Join(dir, "icons"))
		}
	}

	home := os.Getenv("HOME")
	if home != "" {
		if pathExists(filepath.Join(home, ".icons")) {
			dirs = append(dirs, filepath.Join(home, ".icons"))
		}
	}

	exclusions := []string{"default", "hicolor", "locolor"}
	for _, d := range dirs {
		files, err := listFiles(d)
		if err == nil {
			for _, f := range files {
				if f.IsDir() {
					if !isIn(exclusions, f.Name()) {
						content, _ := listFiles(filepath.Join(d, f.Name()))
						if err == nil {
							for _, item := range content {
								if item.Name() == "cursors" {
									name, _, err := iconThemeName(filepath.Join(d, f.Name()))
									if err == nil {
										    name2FolderName[name] = f.Name()
									}
									log.Debugf("Cursor theme found: %s", f.Name())
									name2path[f.Name()] = filepath.Join(d, f.Name(), "cursors")
								}
							}
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return name2path, name2FolderName
}

func getIconThemeNames() map[string]string {
	var dirs []string
	name2folderName := make(map[string]string)

	// get icon theme dirs
	for _, dir := range dataDirs {
		if pathExists(filepath.Join(dir, "icons")) {
			dirs = append(dirs, filepath.Join(dir, "icons"))
		}
	}

	home := os.Getenv("HOME")
	if home != "" {
		if pathExists(filepath.Join(home, ".icons")) {
			dirs = append(dirs, filepath.Join(home, ".icons"))
		}
	}

	exclusions := []string{"default", "hicolor", "locolor"}
	var names []string
	for _, d := range dirs {
		files, err := listFiles(d)
		if err == nil {
			for _, f := range files {
				if f.IsDir() {
					if !isIn(exclusions, f.Name()) {
						name, hasDirs, err := iconThemeName(filepath.Join(d, f.Name()))
						if err == nil && hasDirs {
							names = append(names, name)
							name2folderName[name] = f.Name()
							log.Debugf("Icon theme found: %s", name)
						}
					} else {
						log.Debugf("Excluded icon theme: %s", f.Name())
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	sort.Slice(names, func(i, j int) bool {
		return strings.ToUpper(names[i]) < strings.ToUpper(names[j])
	})

	return name2folderName
}

643	# 4f. Default desktop-content seeding.

699	    # leaves the file untouched when the key is already present.

708	            cur = [line, []]
709	            sections.append(cur)
710	        else:

712	    keyline = key + "=" + value

bool CursorsPage::applyAll() {
  ensureLoaded();
  if (m_pending.empty()) {
    return true;
  }
  for (const auto& [path, value] : m_pending) {
    if (path == themeKeyPath()) {
      if (value.empty()) {
        m_config.removeKey("Appearance", themeGroupKey());
      } else {
        m_config.setString("Appearance", themeGroupKey(), value);
      }
    } else if (path == sizeKeyPath()) {
      int parsed = 0;
      const auto [end, ec] = std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), parsed);
      if (ec == std::errc{} && end == value.data() + value.size()) {
        m_config.setInt("Appearance", sizeGroupKey(), parsed);
      }
    }
  }
  if (!m_config.save()) {
    m_errorNotice = "Failed to write appearance.kwe. Your changes were kept; try Apply again.";
    kLog.warn("kinetic-settings: failed to write {}", m_config.path().string());
    return false;
  }

  // Apply the effective selection system-wide.
  const ThemeValue theme = effectiveTheme();
  const SizeValue size = effectiveSize();
  std::string error;
  if (!applyTheme(theme, size, &error)) {
    m_errorNotice = "Failed to apply the cursor theme: " + error;
    kLog.warn("kinetic-settings: failed to apply cursor theme: {}", error);
    return false;
  }

  m_pending.clear();
  m_errorNotice.clear();
  return true;
}

# Plan: LGL KWE Look — one Qt6 app replacing nwg-look + qt5ct + qt6ct

## Context

`/development/projects/lgl-kwe-look/source/` holds three separate appearance tools:

| Tool | Stack | What it configures |
|---|---|---|
| `nwg-look` 1.1.1 | Go + GTK3 (gotk3) | GTK theme / icons / cursor / font via `gsettings`, exports `settings.ini`, `gtkrc-2.0`, `xsettingsd.conf`, `~/.icons/default/index.theme`, GTK4 symlinks, Flatpak overrides |
| `qt5ct` 1.9 | C++ / Qt5 | `~/.config/qt5ct/qt5ct.conf` (style, palette, fonts, icons, interface, QSS, troubleshooting) + platform-theme plugin + proxy-style plugin |
| `qt6ct` 0.10 | C++ / Qt6 | same, for Qt6 (`qt6ct.conf`) |

Goal: a single native **Qt6 Widgets** app that covers all three, with the look and feel of `/development/projects/lgl-system-loadout` (native Qt widgets, KDE-style page header with title + subtitle, `StyledPanel` frames, green/orange `[Installed]`/`[Not Installed]` badges, palette-aware colours, +2pt base font, monospace log panel, MIT, COPR/RPM packaging, `-Werror` + ASan/UBSan builds, CodeQL/flawfinder workflows).

Project name (assumed, following the directory): **LGL KWE Look**, binary `lgl-kwe-look`, app id `com.linuxgamerlife.lgl-kwe-look`.

## Decisions

Confirmed by you:
- **KineticWE-only.** Target is a KineticWE session on Fedora 44 (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KineticWE`, `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct` exported by the session). `~/.config/kineticwe/appearance.kwe` is the source of truth for icon and cursor theme. The app hides or locks what the session owns.
- **GTK preview = offscreen GTK3 render helper.** A small separate GTK3 binary renders the preview widgets to PNG. The Qt app displays the image.

Assumed (you did not answer these; say so if you want them changed):
- **Config UI only.** The app edits `qt5ct.conf` / `qt6ct.conf` and relies on Fedora's `qt5ct` + `qt6ct` packages for the runtime plugins. KineticWE already lists both as runtime deps (`install-runtime-deps.sh:93-94`). We do **not** rebuild `libqt6ct.so`, `libqt6ct-style.so` or the Qt5 plugins.
- **Sidebar + stacked pages** instead of the benchmark's linear `QWizard`. Each page keeps the benchmark's header (title + subtitle) and frame/badge styling. Apply and Close go in a footer bar.
- **No privileged helper / polkit.** Every write is under `$HOME` or via user-level `gsettings`, so the benchmark's `pkexec` helper, socket IPC and `.policy` file are dropped.

## Architecture

```
lgl-kwe-look/
  CMakeLists.txt        # C++17, AUTOMOC/AUTOUIC/AUTORCC, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, ASan+UBSan in Debug (copy from benchmark)
  src/
    main.cpp            # QApplication, org LinuxGamerLife, +2pt font; do NOT force QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde
    mainwindow.*        # sidebar (QListWidget) + QStackedWidget + footer (Apply/Close/pending indicator/result log)
    pagehelpers.h       # ported from benchmark: SmoothScrollArea, makeItemRow (badge), makeToolbarBtn, makeDescLabel, runChecksAsync
    core/
      kwepaths          # KWE_CONFIG_HOME (~/.config/kineticwe) vs real config home; session detection
      inifile           # line-preserving INI/KConfig patcher + atomic write (port of session script's _ensure()/patch())
      gsettingsclient   # QProcess arg-list wrapper (no shell) + read-back verification
      themescan         # GTK/icon/cursor theme discovery (port of getThemeNames/getIconThemeNames/getCursorThemes)
      xcursor           # native Xcursor -> QImage decoder (replaces xcur2png)
      gtkexport         # settings.ini (3.0/4.0), gtkrc-2.0, xsettingsd.conf, index.theme  [safe-write policy below]
      flatpak           # overrides + port of stylepak (MPL-2.0 derived)
      qtct              # unified Qt5/Qt6 config API: QtTarget{Qt5,Qt6} -> conf path, colors/qss dirs, palette role count
      applypipeline     # ordered sinks, per-sink OK/warn result, single Apply
    pages/
      overview, icons, cursors                 # top level: shared across GTK/Qt5/Qt6, single source of truth
      gtk/   theme, fonts, other, flatpak-export
      qt/    appearance, fonts, interface, stylesheets, troubleshooting   # ONE class set, instantiated per QtTarget
  helpers/gtk-preview/  # separate GTK3 binary (C++17 + GTK3 C API via pkg-config): offscreen render -> PNG, long-lived, stdin line protocol
  colors/ qss/ translations/ packaging/   # from qt6ct + benchmark packaging
```

Key design points:
1. **Icons and cursors are top-level pages, not per toolkit.** In a KWE session one choice must reach every sink at once (see Issue 3), so Apply mirrors what Kinetic Settings does today (`kinetic-settings/src/cursors_page.cpp:190-254`, `icons_page.cpp:254-300`):
   `appearance.kwe [Appearance]` → `kineticwe.kwe [Mouse] cursorTheme/cursorSize` (what the compositor reads) → `kdeglobals [Icons]/[KDE]` → `qt5ct.conf` + `qt6ct.conf` `icon_theme` → `gsettings` icon-theme / cursor-theme / cursor-size → `~/.icons/default/index.theme` → `org.kde.KGlobalSettings.notifyChange` (type 5 for cursors).
2. **One Qt page set, two targets.** The vendored qt5ct and qt6ct pages are structurally identical, so each page takes a `QtTarget`. A "Link Qt5 and Qt6 settings" toggle (default on) writes both files, which matches how the session treats them.
3. **Qt5 target is edited from a Qt6 process.** The style list and platform-theme list for Qt5 come from scanning `/usr/lib64/qt5/plugins/{styles,platformthemes}`, not `QStyleFactory` / `QPlatformThemeFactory`. This also removes the need for `Qt6::GuiPrivate` in the UI. The preview uses the same-named Qt6 style, or Fusion with an "approximate preview" label.
4. **Palette-managed-by-Noctalia.** `colors/noctalia.conf` is shown as "Noctalia (live)" and is read-only: no rename, delete or edit. Choosing another scheme is allowed with a warning. `standard_dialogs` is locked to `xdgdesktopportal` (the session forces it).
5. **Own window state** goes in `~/.config/lgl-kwe-look/`, not in `qt6ct.conf` (upstream saves `SettingsWindow/geometry` there; the plugin's `QFileSystemWatcher` then reloads every running Qt app on every close).
6. **Strings:** keep `tr()` everywhere. Vendor the ~35 qt6ct `.ts` files and convert nwg-look's 10 JSON vocabularies to `.ts` with a script, so there is one translation mechanism. (The benchmark hard-codes English.)

## Milestones

- **M0 Scaffold:** CMake (benchmark flags), main window shell with sidebar, `pagehelpers.h` port, icons/desktop/metainfo/spec skeleton, benchmark `.github` workflows, `LICENSES/`.
- **M1 Core + tests (QtTest):** `inifile` (parity with the session's Python patcher), `gsettingsclient`, `themescan`, `xcursor`, `gtkexport` with golden files generated by real nwg-look on identical input, `qtct` config and palette I/O.
- **M2 Vertical slice:** Icons + Cursors pages and `ApplyPipeline` with all KWE sinks and live notify.
- **M3 GTK pages:** Theme, Fonts, Other, Flatpak/Export + `gtk-preview` helper.
- **M4 Qt pages:** Appearance (palette editor, QSS), Fonts, Interface, Style Sheets, Troubleshooting. Qt6 target first, then Qt5, then linked mode.
- **M5 Parity + migration:** CLI flags `--apply/-a`, `--export/-x`, `--restore-defaults/-r`, `-v`; one-time import of `~/.config/nwg-look/config` and `~/.local/share/nwg-look/gsettings`; i18n.
- **M6 Packaging:** spec (`Requires: qt6-qtbase qt6-qtsvg qt5ct qt6ct gtk3 dconf gsettings-desktop-schemas`), AppStream, COPR via SCM like the benchmark.
- **M7 Hardening:** `-Werror` cleanup of vendored code, ASan/UBSan, CodeQL, flawfinder, VM test matrix.

## Potential issues (ranked)

**High**
1. **Plugins cannot be merged into a Qt6 app.** `libqt5ct.so` / `libqt6ct.so` and the style plugins are loaded into *other* processes, are locked to one Qt major, link Qt private APIs (`GuiPrivate`, `qgenericunixthemes_p.h`, `qiconloader_p.h`), and refuse to load unless `QLibraryInfo::version()` major.minor equals the build version (`qt6ct-qtplugin/main.cpp`). "Covers all three apps" therefore means the *configuration UIs*, not the runtime plugins. If you later want our own plugins, that is a separate Qt5 sub-build plus a rebuild on every Qt minor bump.
2. **nwg-look's GTK4 export would break Noctalia's GTK colours.** `clearGtk4Symlinks()` (`tools.go:941`) deletes `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-dark.css`, `assets`, `~/.config/assets` and `gtk-4.0/settings.ini`, then symlinks the theme's files. Noctalia's `templates/gtk/apply.sh` keeps regular `gtk-3.0/gtk.css` and `gtk-4.0/gtk.css` files containing `@import noctalia.css`. nwg-look defaults `ExportGtk4Symlinks=true`. Port rule: never delete or replace a regular file, only symlinks we created; default the GTK4 export off in KWE mode; never touch `gtk.css` or `noctalia.css`.
3. **Several existing writers own the same keys.** `start-kineticwe.sh` step 4h rewrites `icon_theme` (from `appearance.kwe` / `kdeglobals`) and legacy `standard_dialogs` in both `qt*ct.conf` files at **every login**; Kinetic Settings' Icons and Cursors pages write `appearance.kwe`, `kineticwe.kwe`, `kdeglobals`, gsettings and `qt*ct.conf`. If we only write `qt6ct.conf`, the icon theme silently reverts at next login. We must write the same sink set (Design point 1), idempotently. Consider deep-linking to Kinetic Settings for Icons/Cursors instead of duplicating them; that is your call.
4. **GTK live preview needs GTK3 after all.** The helper adds a `gtk3-devel` build dep, a `gtk3` runtime dep and a second binary, and it needs a live display (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`). It must set `gtk-theme-name` / dark preference / font before creating widgets, honour HiDPI scale, and be long-lived (a per-click spawn is slow). GTK3 headers are noisy under `-Werror` (deprecations), so that target needs `-Wno-deprecated-declarations`. libadwaita-style themes (`adw-gtk3`) must be installed to preview.
5. **Source snapshots are out of step.** Vendored qt5ct is 1.9 and has the "reworked color settings" (Default / Style's colors, `style-colors.conf`, system-palette handling). Vendored qt6ct is an older 0.10 without it (its palette code differs and `writeSettings` takes a `QSettings*`). Fedora's installed qt6ct 0.11 lists "reworked color settings" in its changelog, and its ChangeLog says the home moved to opencode.net, while the vendored README still points at GitHub. Use qt5ct 1.9 as the functional baseline, port the Qt6-specific bits (`QPalette::Accent`, `textActivated`, `QThread` loader) from qt6ct, and diff against the installed 0.11 before trusting the vendored copy.
6. **Config compatibility with the *installed* plugins.** Keys we write must match what Fedora's 1.9 / 0.11 plugins read (`custom_palette`, `color_scheme_path`, `style`, `standard_dialogs`, `icon_theme`, `[Fonts]`, `[Interface]`, `[Troubleshooting]`). `QPalette::Accent` (Qt 6.6+) makes Qt6 palettes 22 roles vs Qt5's 21; scheme files shared between the two need explicit role-count adaptation. Needs tests against real plugin behaviour, not just our own reader.
7. **Licensing.** nwg-look and the benchmark are MIT; qt5ct/qt6ct are BSD-2-Clause (notices must be kept in source and binary docs); `stylepak` is a Go translation of MPL-2.0 code, so a C++ port stays MPL-2.0 at file level. Needs a `LICENSES/` tree and `%license` entries, and you should pick the overall project licence.

**Medium**
8. **`gsettings` can fail silently.** Without a session bus / dconf, the backend falls back to memory and writes appear to succeed. nwg-look never verifies. Read every key back after writing. Use argument lists, never a shell (matches the benchmark's rule).
9. **qt*ct.conf is edited concurrently** (our app, the login script's atomic `os.replace`, and the plugin's file watcher in every running Qt app). Do read-modify-write of only changed keys with `QSaveFile`; do not hold a `QSettings` open. Note that every save triggers a live theme reload in all running Qt apps.
10. **Qt5 target fidelity.** A Qt6 process cannot instantiate Qt5 styles, so the Qt5 style preview is approximate. Qt5 plugin directory is distro-specific (`/usr/lib64/qt5/plugins` on Fedora). Qt5 is being wound down in distros, so verify it is still shipped on Fedora 44/45 (qt5ct 1.9 is installed here today).
11. **Behaviour drift in the Go → C++ port** (~2k lines: `tools.go` + `uicomponents.go`). Mitigate with golden-file tests against real nwg-look output (M1).
12. **Cursor preview dependency.** nwg-look shells out to `xcur2png`. A native Xcursor decoder (~100 lines) removes that dependency; animated and multi-size cursors need handling.
13. **Look-and-feel carry-overs to avoid or adapt.** The benchmark forces `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde` when unset, but a KWE session has no Plasma platform plugin (it uses `qt5ct`), so do not force it. Under `qt5ct` the tool also restyles itself live from the file it edits; previews must set style and palette explicitly on the preview subtree (qt6ct's `previewform` already does). The benchmark's `setMinimumSize(1100, 1000)` is too big for small screens; use ~1000×700. Its hard-coded hex colours are not dark/light aware (keep the badge colours, use palette tokens elsewhere).
14. **Toolchain.** This host has no `cmake`, `gcc`, `go` or Qt devel packages; the benchmark builds inside the `fedora-dev1` distrobox. The benchmark pins **C++17** (Qt 6.10 header issue on Fedora 43+) and `-Werror`; vendored qt6ct will need a warnings cleanup pass. Qt6 components needed: Core, Widgets, Concurrent, DBus, Svg (runtime), LinguistTools.

**Low**
15. **Coexistence.** The distro `nwg-look`, `qt5ct`, `qt6ct` desktop entries remain installed and write the same files. No file conflicts, but users can edit from two tools; use `Requires` for the plugin packages, not `Conflicts`.
16. **`flatpak override --env=ICON_THEME`** (carried over from nwg-look) is not a standard variable; keep as an opt-in, default off, like nwg-look.
17. **Working agreements** (from your loadout `MEMORY.md`): use absolute paths (`cd` is aliased to `z`), do not run builds or git unless told, and omit the `Co-Authored-By` trailer for this repo unless you say otherwise.

## Verification (later, in a KineticWE VM session)

- QtTest unit tests: `inifile` patcher parity with the session's Python; palette role adaptation (21 ↔ 22); gsettings read-back; GTK export golden files vs nwg-look output.
- After Apply, check: `appearance.kwe`, `kineticwe.kwe [Mouse]`, `kdeglobals`, `gsettings get …`, `qt5ct.conf` / `qt6ct.conf` `icon_theme`. Then re-run the login sync (step 4h) and confirm nothing reverts.
- Checksums of `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-3.0/gtk.css` and `colors/noctalia.conf` are unchanged after Apply in every GTK export mode.
- A running Qt5 app, Qt6 app, GTK3 app and GTK4 app all restyle live; cursor changes reload in the compositor.
- `gtk-preview` renders under Wayland; check dark/light and HiDPI.
- Debug build with ASan + UBSan, CodeQL and flawfinder clean; visual side-by-side with a benchmark screenshot.

## Open items for you

- Confirm or change the two assumed decisions (config-UI-only, sidebar navigation).
- Overall project licence.
- Whether Icons and Cursors should be full pages here or deep-links into Kinetic Settings.

| Tool | Stack | What it configures |
|---|---|---|
| `nwg-look` 1.1.1 | Go + GTK3 (gotk3) | GTK theme / icons / cursor / font via `gsettings`, exports `settings.ini`, `gtkrc-2.0`, `xsettingsd.conf`, `~/.icons/default/index.theme`, GTK4 symlinks, Flatpak overrides |
| `qt5ct` 1.9 | C++ / Qt5 | `~/.config/qt5ct/qt5ct.conf` (style, palette, fonts, icons, interface, QSS, troubleshooting) + platform-theme plugin + proxy-style plugin |
| `qt6ct` 0.10 | C++ / Qt6 | same, for Qt6 (`qt6ct.conf`) |

Goal: a single native **Qt6 Widgets** app that covers all three, with the look and feel of `/development/projects/lgl-system-loadout` (native Qt widgets, KDE-style page header with title + subtitle, `StyledPanel` frames, green/orange `[Installed]`/`[Not Installed]` badges, palette-aware colours, +2pt base font, monospace log panel, MIT, COPR/RPM packaging, `-Werror` + ASan/UBSan builds, CodeQL/flawfinder workflows).

Project name (assumed, following the directory): **LGL KWE Look**, binary `lgl-kwe-look`, app id `com.linuxgamerlife.lgl-kwe-look`.

## Decisions

Confirmed by you:
- **KineticWE-only.** Target is a KineticWE session on Fedora 44 (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KineticWE`, `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct` exported by the session). `~/.config/kineticwe/appearance.kwe` is the source of truth for icon and cursor theme. The app hides or locks what the session owns.
- **GTK preview = offscreen GTK3 render helper.** A small separate GTK3 binary renders the preview widgets to PNG. The Qt app displays the image.

Assumed (you did not answer these; say so if you want them changed):
- **Config UI only.** The app edits `qt5ct.conf` / `qt6ct.conf` and relies on Fedora's `qt5ct` + `qt6ct` packages for the runtime plugins. KineticWE already lists both as runtime deps (`install-runtime-deps.sh:93-94`). We do **not** rebuild `libqt6ct.so`, `libqt6ct-style.so` or the Qt5 plugins.
- **Sidebar + stacked pages** instead of the benchmark's linear `QWizard`. Each page keeps the benchmark's header (title + subtitle) and frame/badge styling. Apply and Close go in a footer bar.
- **No privileged helper / polkit.** Every write is under `$HOME` or via user-level `gsettings`, so the benchmark's `pkexec` helper, socket IPC and `.policy` file are dropped.

## Architecture

```
lgl-kwe-look/
  CMakeLists.txt        # C++17, AUTOMOC/AUTOUIC/AUTORCC, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, ASan+UBSan in Debug (copy from benchmark)
  src/
    main.cpp            # QApplication, org LinuxGamerLife, +2pt font; do NOT force QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde
    mainwindow.*        # sidebar (QListWidget) + QStackedWidget + footer (Apply/Close/pending indicator/result log)
    pagehelpers.h       # ported from benchmark: SmoothScrollArea, makeItemRow (badge), makeToolbarBtn, makeDescLabel, runChecksAsync
    core/
      kwepaths          # KWE_CONFIG_HOME (~/.config/kineticwe) vs real config home; session detection
      inifile           # line-preserving INI/KConfig patcher + atomic write (port of session script's _ensure()/patch())
      gsettingsclient   # QProcess arg-list wrapper (no shell) + read-back verification
      themescan         # GTK/icon/cursor theme discovery (port of getThemeNames/getIconThemeNames/getCursorThemes)
      xcursor           # native Xcursor -> QImage decoder (replaces xcur2png)
      gtkexport         # settings.ini (3.0/4.0), gtkrc-2.0, xsettingsd.conf, index.theme  [safe-write policy below]
      flatpak           # overrides + port of stylepak (MPL-2.0 derived)
      qtct              # unified Qt5/Qt6 config API: QtTarget{Qt5,Qt6} -> conf path, colors/qss dirs, palette role count
      applypipeline     # ordered sinks, per-sink OK/warn result, single Apply
    pages/
      overview, icons, cursors                 # top level: shared across GTK/Qt5/Qt6, single source of truth
      gtk/   theme, fonts, other, flatpak-export
      qt/    appearance, fonts, interface, stylesheets, troubleshooting   # ONE class set, instantiated per QtTarget
  helpers/gtk-preview/  # separate GTK3 binary (C++17 + GTK3 C API via pkg-config): offscreen render -> PNG, long-lived, stdin line protocol
  colors/ qss/ translations/ packaging/   # from qt6ct + benchmark packaging
```

Key design points:
1. **Icons and cursors are top-level pages, not per toolkit.** In a KWE session one choice must reach every sink at once (see Issue 3), so Apply mirrors what Kinetic Settings does today (`kinetic-settings/src/cursors_page.cpp:190-254`, `icons_page.cpp:254-300`):
   `appearance.kwe [Appearance]` → `kineticwe.kwe [Mouse] cursorTheme/cursorSize` (what the compositor reads) → `kdeglobals [Icons]/[KDE]` → `qt5ct.conf` + `qt6ct.conf` `icon_theme` → `gsettings` icon-theme / cursor-theme / cursor-size → `~/.icons/default/index.theme` → `org.kde.KGlobalSettings.notifyChange` (type 5 for cursors).
2. **One Qt page set, two targets.** The vendored qt5ct and qt6ct pages are structurally identical, so each page takes a `QtTarget`. A "Link Qt5 and Qt6 settings" toggle (default on) writes both files, which matches how the session treats them.
3. **Qt5 target is edited from a Qt6 process.** The style list and platform-theme list for Qt5 come from scanning `/usr/lib64/qt5/plugins/{styles,platformthemes}`, not `QStyleFactory` / `QPlatformThemeFactory`. This also removes the need for `Qt6::GuiPrivate` in the UI. The preview uses the same-named Qt6 style, or Fusion with an "approximate preview" label.
4. **Palette-managed-by-Noctalia.** `colors/noctalia.conf` is shown as "Noctalia (live)" and is read-only: no rename, delete or edit. Choosing another scheme is allowed with a warning. `standard_dialogs` is locked to `xdgdesktopportal` (the session forces it).
5. **Own window state** goes in `~/.config/lgl-kwe-look/`, not in `qt6ct.conf` (upstream saves `SettingsWindow/geometry` there; the plugin's `QFileSystemWatcher` then reloads every running Qt app on every close).
6. **Strings:** keep `tr()` everywhere. Vendor the ~35 qt6ct `.ts` files and convert nwg-look's 10 JSON vocabularies to `.ts` with a script, so there is one translation mechanism. (The benchmark hard-codes English.)

## Milestones

- **M0 Scaffold:** CMake (benchmark flags), main window shell with sidebar, `pagehelpers.h` port, icons/desktop/metainfo/spec skeleton, benchmark `.github` workflows, `LICENSES/`.
- **M1 Core + tests (QtTest):** `inifile` (parity with the session's Python patcher), `gsettingsclient`, `themescan`, `xcursor`, `gtkexport` with golden files generated by real nwg-look on identical input, `qtct` config and palette I/O.
- **M2 Vertical slice:** Icons + Cursors pages and `ApplyPipeline` with all KWE sinks and live notify.
- **M3 GTK pages:** Theme, Fonts, Other, Flatpak/Export + `gtk-preview` helper.
- **M4 Qt pages:** Appearance (palette editor, QSS), Fonts, Interface, Style Sheets, Troubleshooting. Qt6 target first, then Qt5, then linked mode.
- **M5 Parity + migration:** CLI flags `--apply/-a`, `--export/-x`, `--restore-defaults/-r`, `-v`; one-time import of `~/.config/nwg-look/config` and `~/.local/share/nwg-look/gsettings`; i18n.
- **M6 Packaging:** spec (`Requires: qt6-qtbase qt6-qtsvg qt5ct qt6ct gtk3 dconf gsettings-desktop-schemas`), AppStream, COPR via SCM like the benchmark.
- **M7 Hardening:** `-Werror` cleanup of vendored code, ASan/UBSan, CodeQL, flawfinder, VM test matrix.

## Potential issues (ranked)

**High**
1. **Plugins cannot be merged into a Qt6 app.** `libqt5ct.so` / `libqt6ct.so` and the style plugins are loaded into *other* processes, are locked to one Qt major, link Qt private APIs (`GuiPrivate`, `qgenericunixthemes_p.h`, `qiconloader_p.h`), and refuse to load unless `QLibraryInfo::version()` major.minor equals the build version (`qt6ct-qtplugin/main.cpp`). "Covers all three apps" therefore means the *configuration UIs*, not the runtime plugins. If you later want our own plugins, that is a separate Qt5 sub-build plus a rebuild on every Qt minor bump.
2. **nwg-look's GTK4 export would break Noctalia's GTK colours.** `clearGtk4Symlinks()` (`tools.go:941`) deletes `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-dark.css`, `assets`, `~/.config/assets` and `gtk-4.0/settings.ini`, then symlinks the theme's files. Noctalia's `templates/gtk/apply.sh` keeps regular `gtk-3.0/gtk.css` and `gtk-4.0/gtk.css` files containing `@import noctalia.css`. nwg-look defaults `ExportGtk4Symlinks=true`. Port rule: never delete or replace a regular file, only symlinks we created; default the GTK4 export off in KWE mode; never touch `gtk.css` or `noctalia.css`.
3. **Several existing writers own the same keys.** `start-kineticwe.sh` step 4h rewrites `icon_theme` (from `appearance.kwe` / `kdeglobals`) and legacy `standard_dialogs` in both `qt*ct.conf` files at **every login**; Kinetic Settings' Icons and Cursors pages write `appearance.kwe`, `kineticwe.kwe`, `kdeglobals`, gsettings and `qt*ct.conf`. If we only write `qt6ct.conf`, the icon theme silently reverts at next login. We must write the same sink set (Design point 1), idempotently. Consider deep-linking to Kinetic Settings for Icons/Cursors instead of duplicating them; that is your call.
4. **GTK live preview needs GTK3 after all.** The helper adds a `gtk3-devel` build dep, a `gtk3` runtime dep and a second binary, and it needs a live display (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`). It must set `gtk-theme-name` / dark preference / font before creating widgets, honour HiDPI scale, and be long-lived (a per-click spawn is slow). GTK3 headers are noisy under `-Werror` (deprecations), so that target needs `-Wno-deprecated-declarations`. libadwaita-style themes (`adw-gtk3`) must be installed to preview.
5. **Source snapshots are out of step.** Vendored qt5ct is 1.9 and has the "reworked color settings" (Default / Style's colors, `style-colors.conf`, system-palette handling). Vendored qt6ct is an older 0.10 without it (its palette code differs and `writeSettings` takes a `QSettings*`). Fedora's installed qt6ct 0.11 lists "reworked color settings" in its changelog, and its ChangeLog says the home moved to opencode.net, while the vendored README still points at GitHub. Use qt5ct 1.9 as the functional baseline, port the Qt6-specific bits (`QPalette::Accent`, `textActivated`, `QThread` loader) from qt6ct, and diff against the installed 0.11 before trusting the vendored copy.
6. **Config compatibility with the *installed* plugins.** Keys we write must match what Fedora's 1.9 / 0.11 plugins read (`custom_palette`, `color_scheme_path`, `style`, `standard_dialogs`, `icon_theme`, `[Fonts]`, `[Interface]`, `[Troubleshooting]`). `QPalette::Accent` (Qt 6.6+) makes Qt6 palettes 22 roles vs Qt5's 21; scheme files shared between the two need explicit role-count adaptation. Needs tests against real plugin behaviour, not just our own reader.
7. **Licensing.** nwg-look and the benchmark are MIT; qt5ct/qt6ct are BSD-2-Clause (notices must be kept in source and binary docs); `stylepak` is a Go translation of MPL-2.0 code, so a C++ port stays MPL-2.0 at file level. Needs a `LICENSES/` tree and `%license` entries, and you should pick the overall project licence.

**Medium**
8. **`gsettings` can fail silently.** Without a session bus / dconf, the backend falls back to memory and writes appear to succeed. nwg-look never verifies. Read every key back after writing. Use argument lists, never a shell (matches the benchmark's rule).
9. **qt*ct.conf is edited concurrently** (our app, the login script's atomic `os.replace`, and the plugin's file watcher in every running Qt app). Do read-modify-write of only changed keys with `QSaveFile`; do not hold a `QSettings` open. Note that every save triggers a live theme reload in all running Qt apps.
10. **Qt5 target fidelity.** A Qt6 process cannot instantiate Qt5 styles, so the Qt5 style preview is approximate. Qt5 plugin directory is distro-specific (`/usr/lib64/qt5/plugins` on Fedora). Qt5 is being wound down in distros, so verify it is still shipped on Fedora 44/45 (qt5ct 1.9 is installed here today).
11. **Behaviour drift in the Go → C++ port** (~2k lines: `tools.go` + `uicomponents.go`). Mitigate with golden-file tests against real nwg-look output (M1).
12. **Cursor preview dependency.** nwg-look shells out to `xcur2png`. A native Xcursor decoder (~100 lines) removes that dependency; animated and multi-size cursors need handling.
13. **Look-and-feel carry-overs to avoid or adapt.** The benchmark forces `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde` when unset, but a KWE session has no Plasma platform plugin (it uses `qt5ct`), so do not force it. Under `qt5ct` the tool also restyles itself live from the file it edits; previews must set style and palette explicitly on the preview subtree (qt6ct's `previewform` already does). The benchmark's `setMinimumSize(1100, 1000)` is too big for small screens; use ~1000×700. Its hard-coded hex colours are not dark/light aware (keep the badge colours, use palette tokens elsewhere).
14. **Toolchain.** This host has no `cmake`, `gcc`, `go` or Qt devel packages; the benchmark builds inside the `fedora-dev1` distrobox. The benchmark pins **C++17** (Qt 6.10 header issue on Fedora 43+) and `-Werror`; vendored qt6ct will need a warnings cleanup pass. Qt6 components needed: Core, Widgets, Concurrent, DBus, Svg (runtime), LinguistTools.

**Low**
15. **Coexistence.** The distro `nwg-look`, `qt5ct`, `qt6ct` desktop entries remain installed and write the same files. No file conflicts, but users can edit from two tools; use `Requires` for the plugin packages, not `Conflicts`.
16. **`flatpak override --env=ICON_THEME`** (carried over from nwg-look) is not a standard variable; keep as an opt-in, default off, like nwg-look.
17. **Working agreements** (from your loadout `MEMORY.md`): use absolute paths (`cd` is aliased to `z`), do not run builds or git unless told, and omit the `Co-Authored-By` trailer for this repo unless you say otherwise.

## Environment

- Dev work happens inside the `fedora-dev1` distrobox (Fedora 44 toolbox-style container).
- Host root is bind-mounted at `/run/host/` inside the container, so the repo is reachable there at
  `/run/host/development/projects/lgl-system-loadout`. From the host it's just
  `/development/projects/lgl-system-loadout`.
- Build with `cmake --build build --parallel` (from repo root, inside the distrobox).
- Host also has ImageMagick (`magick`/`convert`/`identify`) — image/text edits can be done directly
  on the host; C++ builds should go through `fedora-dev1` to match the target platform.
- **Gotcha**: `~/.bashrc` has `alias cd=z` (zoxide). In non-interactive shells this breaks `cd`
  silently (`z: command not found`, directory doesn't change). Use absolute paths, avoid relying on `cd`.
- No `gh` CLI installed. GitHub issues/releases/tags read via the public REST API
  (`curl https://api.github.com/repos/linuxgamerlife/lgl-system-loadout/...`), no auth needed for
  public read access.
- `origin` remote is SSH (`git@github.com:linuxgamerlife/lgl-system-loadout.git`). SSH key auth
  confirmed working (key added to GitHub account as "fedora-dev1", unlocked via
  `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` — needs the passphrase entered manually each time the agent doesn't
  already hold it).
- **The installed app (Discover / app menu / COPR) is a separate copy from `build/`.** The
  privileged helper in particular is a fixed system path
  (`/usr/libexec/lgl-system-loadout/lgl-system-loadout-helper`) launched by `pkexec` — rebuilding
  locally does *not* update it. To test helper/GUI changes against the real running app:
  ```
  sudo cp build/lgl-system-loadout /usr/local/bin/lgl-system-loadout
  sudo cp build/lgl-system-loadout-helper /usr/libexec/lgl-system-loadout/lgl-system-loadout-helper
  ```
  Only copy whichever binary actually changed (GUI vs. helper) — check the diff first.
- **Privileged helper architecture constraint** (important for any future update-flow work): the
  helper's `QLocalServer` only ever accepts **one client connection for its entire process
  lifetime** (`helperserver.cpp` calls `m_server.close()` right after accepting the first client),
  and the whole helper process quits the moment that client disconnects
  (`sessionEnded → QCoreApplication::quit` in `helper/main.cpp`). `InstallWorker::run()` always
  sends `"shutdown"` and disconnects at the end of its run. This means **you cannot split one
  logical "session" across two separate `InstallWorker::run()` calls reusing the same socket path**
  — the first call's normal completion kills the helper. Each additional phase needs its own
  `m_wiz->launchHelper()` call (a fresh `pkexec` prompt each time, since the polkit policy disables
  credential caching). Got bitten by this once already (see "Work completed" below).
- Repo is on branch `main` (user merged `dev` into `main` and pushed themselves). Current app version
  is **2.0.3**, committed and pushed to `main` (GitHub Release/tag not yet created as of end of this
  session — user creates those themselves).
- COPR project builds via SCM (rpkg method, `Committish` blank → tracks `main` directly, no tag
  needed). **Gotcha hit this session**: COPR kept building the old version because the version-bump
  commit was made locally but not yet pushed — `git status` showing "ahead of origin/main by N
  commits" is the tell. COPR can only see what's actually on GitHub.
- User tests this app in a **VM**, not on this host/distrobox — I have no visibility into that VM.
  Do not run system-inspection commands (`flatpak list`, checking installed binaries, etc.) against
  *this* machine and present the results as if they reflect the user's test environment — got
  corrected firmly on this. Diagnose purely from source when the user is testing elsewhere, and ask
  the user to run/paste specific commands themselves when live system state is needed.
